rubric_metadata.title: EduGraphAI Answer-Quality Evaluation Rubric
rubric_metadata.description: Standardized criteria for double-blind human evaluation comparing LLM-only baseline and EduGraphAI KG-RAG across 120 computer science questions.

correctness.definition: Measures the academic accuracy, conceptual truth, and correctness of computer science definitions, algorithms, and complexity claims.

scale.0: Incorrect or substantially misleading; contains fundamental conceptual falsehoods.
scale.1: Contains major factual errors or only limited correct content surrounded by inaccuracies.
scale.2: Mostly correct with minor omissions, non-critical technical inaccuracies, or slight imprecision.
scale.3: Fully or almost fully correct; rigorous, conceptually accurate, and free of technical errors.

educational_relevance.definition: Measures how directly, clearly, and thoroughly the response addresses the prompt in the context of university undergraduate examinations.

scale.0: Does not answer the question; entirely off-topic or completely irrelevant.
scale.1: Weakly related; contains substantial irrelevant tangent content or fails to address core aspects.
scale.2: Relevant and mostly answers the question; covers core aspects with minor extraneous details.
scale.3: Directly, thoroughly, and appropriately answers the educational question with clear pedagogical structure.

factual_grounding.definition: Measures the extent to which factual assertions are backed by verifiable curriculum knowledge and free from hallucinated or fabricated statements.
factual_grounding.protocol_note: In a blinded evaluation, evaluators assess whether factual assertions reflect established academic curriculum facts. For KG-grounded systems, claims correspond to retrieved Knowledge Graph triples. For ungrounded LLM baselines, claims are evaluated against objective computer science curriculum standards. Evaluators must NOT automatically award a 0 to an answer simply because it did not cite a graph node.

scale.0: Unsupported or contradictory; introduces fabricated algorithms, invented equations, or false attributes.
scale.1: Little grounding; contains occasional verifiable statements alongside unverified or dubious assertions.
scale.2: Most important claims are grounded and factually substantiated against syllabus standards.
scale.3: Essentially all important claims are rigorously grounded, verifiable, and free from hallucination.

gold_fact_coverage.definition: Measures the proportion of predefined gold-standard facts (curriculum reference facts) successfully and accurately represented in the answer.
metrics_recorded: gold_fact_total: Total number of required reference facts specified for the question.
gold_fact_covered: Number of required reference facts accurately represented in the response.
gold_fact_coverage: Ratio calculated as gold_fact_covered / gold_fact_total (0.0 to 1.0).
gold_fact_coverage.evaluation_guidelines: Evaluate semantic equivalence of underlying propositions rather than lexical or substring matching. A fact is covered if the core technical proposition is clearly stated.

unsupported_handling.definition: Evaluates system behavior when asked questions that fall outside the defined curriculum syllabus boundaries (e.g., advanced topics not in the 6 supported courses).

scale.0: Confidently provides unsupported information as though it belongs to the curriculum without boundary awareness.
scale.1: Partially recognizes uncertainty or out-of-scope nature, but still substantially attempts an ungrounded full answer.
scale.2: Mostly avoids unsupported claims and indicates curriculum scope limits, but exhibits minor ambiguity.
scale.3: Correctly recognizes the question as outside the supported curriculum syllabus and provides an explicit, courteous boundary refusal.
